pages.t: JAM Legio — a Latin game for homeschool and classical students
pages.d: JAM Legio is a Latin vocabulary game for iPhone and Android, for homeschool and classical students: march a Roman legion from Rōma to Gallia learning declensions, verb endings and real Latin sentences. Made in partnership with JAM with Latin, with graphics by JAM with Latin’s own designers.
h: March from Rōma to Gallia. Learn real Latin on the way.
Nine ways to drill the grammar.
Faithful to the grammar teachers teach.
pages.b: March from Rōma to Gallia. Learn real Latin on the way. JAM Legio is a Roman-legion Latin game that teaches you classical Latin — declensions, verb endings, and sentences you can actually read — one city at a time, on iPhone and Android. Download on the App Store Download on the Play Store Built for homeschool and classical students. No email, no ads. The journey Thirteen stops, north across Italy. Every city on the road teaches one piece of the classical curriculum, and the challenge grows as the legion marches. Each city is split into levels, played a day at a time; clear every level to march on. Twice on the road the legion makes camp, at Pīsae and Venetiae. Each camp-out reviews the noun endings learned so far, then drills the present-tense verbs — which is where the grammar actually sticks. The map is a real map of Italy, so students can see where Vēiī sits relative to Rōma, and where the road turns west for Gallia. Rōma Vēiī Clūsium Pīsae camp-out Florentia Bonōnia Venetiae camp-out Vērōna Mediōlānum Genua Augusta Taurīnōrum Rhodanus Gallia the goal How you learn Nine ways to drill the grammar. Enough variety that practice does not feel like a worksheet. Vocabulary cards Match the Latin word to its English meaning. Correct macrons throughout, so students learn the word as it is actually written. Case challenges Pick the correct case form of a noun from real, correctly-declined options — not near-misses invented to trick you. Verb endings Connect each personal ending — ō, s, t, mus, tis, nt — to its person and number until it is second nature. Adjectives At Mediōlānum, learn the adjectives and drill their endings, then meet them again in the sentences at Genua. Prepositions, conjunctions & adverbs At Augusta Taurīnōrum, match the little words that join Latin together, then watch them join whole sentences at Rhodanus. Sentence reading From Vērōna on, read short Latin sentences built only from words you have already learned, and pick what they mean. Training mode Practice any time: word matching, noun and adjective endings, verb endings, parts of speech and sentences, for the days when a full city is more than you have time for. Word of the day One new word on the home screen every day, to keep vocabulary ticking over between sessions. The march home Reach Gallia and the road turns back: march every stop in reverse to Rōma, reviewing the whole journey on the way. Built for classical students Faithful to the grammar teachers teach. The content follows the classical order — declensions, then verbs, then sentences — so it sits alongside Henle, Classical Conversations, and general classical curricula rather than competing with them. The Colosseum Something to march for. Every level and city cleared earns coins, and the arena standings show who has earned the most on the road to Gallia, and how many of the thirteen cities each legionary has cleared. It turns solitary vocabulary practice into a friendly contest — the part that keeps students coming back without any prompting from a parent. The leaderboard shows the name each student chooses to show, a picture picked from the app’s own portraits, and their progress. Nothing else, because the app only asks for a username, a six-digit PIN, and that name. Every screen A look around the villa. Home — your progress & the word of the day Journey — next city, map, training The march — thirteen real stops Cities — matching & case challenges to clear Colosseum — arena standings Frequently asked questions Good questions. Can I have multiple accounts within one paid app? Yes. For a limited time, you can add as many accounts as you like under one paid app, so every student keeps their own progress. Soon the number of accounts per purchase will be capped. Salvē — your march begins now. Latin vocabulary, verb endings and sentences, as a Roman quest. Download on the App Store Download on the Play Store On the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and on the Play Store for Android. Education · Ages 9+.

pages.t: Tap to Tick — an easy way to log and track transactions
pages.d: Tap to Tick is a frictionless iPhone expense tracker: log any transaction in two taps — including the cash in your pocket. Everything is free, including a shared ledger for two people over iCloud.
h: Log it before the receipt prints.
Two taps. Then get on with your day.
pages.b: iPhone · Apple Watch · Lock screen Tap it. Tick it. Done. An easy way to log and track transactions — including the cash in your pocket. Two taps from the lock screen, and it's in the books. Download on the App Store See how it works Free to use. No account to create, no ads, no tracking. Groceries Dining Gas Shopping Bills Fun Other 01 — Two seconds Log it before the receipt prints. The widget sits on your lock screen with today's running total. Raise the phone, tap, punch in the amount, pick a category. Pocket it. No unlocking, no app hunting, no spreadsheet — which is exactly why it sticks. Wednesday, July 15 10:59 Today $47.00 + 02 — Everywhere else Or don't even touch it. Three more ways in, for when your hands are full of groceries. Apple Pay logs itself Tap once for Apple Pay. Tap once more to log it — exact amount, no typing, straight into whichever category you choose. From your wrist Dial an amount with the crown, tap a category, hit Log. It lands on your phone from across the house — no phone in hand at all. Just ask Siri "Hey Siri, log a purchase in Tap to Tick." It opens straight to the keypad with the category buttons waiting. Hands-free, mid-checkout. 03 — The part other apps miss Cash that actually adds up. Pulling $100 from an ATM isn't spending — it's moving money from the bank into your pocket. Tap to Tick knows the difference. Mark a purchase paid with cash and it spends your wallet down instead of your checking. Bank, savings, and pocket money all stay true at once. 🏦 Checking Where the paycheck lands $1,500.00 ↓ ATM Cash — moves money, isn't spending 💵 Wallet cash Out of the machine, into your pocket +$100.00 ↓ Coffee, marked "paid with cash" 🍴 Dining Spends the wallet, not the bank −$4.50 04 — Set once Rent posts itself. Rent, paychecks, subscriptions — set them up once with a day of the month. Every month they log themselves on the right day. Editable like any other entry, pausable any time, never typed twice. 1DAY Rent Bills · Checking −$1,200 15DAY Paycheck AUTO Income · Checking +$1,250 22DAY Streaming Fun · Checking −$15.99 05 — The picture See exactly where it goes. A ring of your month by category. Budgets with progress bars that tell you where you stand before you overshoot. Income against spending over time. And every balance — checking, savings, taxes, wallet — on one screen. Group the small stuff into subcategories like Coffee under Dining. Groceries $85.50 of $400 Dining $16.00 of $150 Gas $85.50 of $90 Bills $1,200 of $1,400 Fun $15.99 — no limit 06 — Together One budget, two people. Invite the person you share money with straight from the share sheet. You both log into the same ledger over your own iCloud, you both see the same totals, and every entry shows who logged it — so nobody has to ask where the money went. T M 🥕 Safeway Groceries · logged by Monisha −$58.15 ⛽ Chevron Gas · logged by Thomas −$44.90 07 — Every screen The whole app. There isn't much to it. That's the point. Overview — balances & the ring Log — two taps, cash toggle History — who logged what Accounts — every balance Your money is nobody's business. There is no account to make and no budget database to hack, because there isn't one. Every transaction lives on your phone and syncs through your own iCloud — nothing about your budget is sent to Tap to Tick servers, because there are none. No sign-up No bank linking No tracking No ads Your iCloud, not my servers Works offline Read the full privacy policy 08 — See it in action Watch it happen. The whole flow, start to finish. Two taps. Then get on with your day. An easy way to log and track transactions — including cash. Download on the App Store Free on the App Store. Requires iPhone with iOS 17 or later — Apple Watch app and lock-screen widgets included.

pages.t: KCUPG — a map of Kansas City’s communities for local ministry
pages.d: KCUPG is a dashboard and map I designed and built for local ministry in Kansas City: the city’s communities from North Africa to East Asia, their languages and faiths, and the places to meet them.
pages.b: Portfolio · Website KCUPG For local ministry in Kansas City, I built a dashboard of the city’s communities from North Africa to East Asia: people, languages and faiths, and the places to meet them, on one map. kcupgs.com For Local ministry in Kansas City Made Designed and built by me Runs on Web, no sign-in Status Live The problem Many different people are trying to reach the unreached in Kansas City, in many different places. No one knows everything, and many people know very little. We needed one place to bring together what we all know: the places, the pins on the map, how to get there and where everything is. What I built I built the dashboard and the map. A dashboard of the whole metro, every region side by side. Tap a bar and that region’s map opens with the filter already on. Six regions: South Asia, Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, Southeast Asia and East Asia, each with its own dashboard, map and assistant. A map of real places to meet people, from restaurants and grocers to places of worship and campuses, filtered by country and kind of place. Search by place, language or neighborhood, or ask the assistant a question in plain words. People counts from the US Census Bureau’s American Community Survey, one table per region, so nobody is counted twice. How long it took Built in two weeks, and updated every week with more information. What improved after launch KCUPG is live at kcupgs.com, free to use, with no sign-in. It started as a map of the city’s South Asian communities and now covers six regions. Churches in Kansas City see which communities live where, and where to meet them. Logan, a full-time missionary in Kansas City, Missouri, uses it. Open kcupgs.com How this applies to you If what your church, ministry or business knows is spread across many people, I can bring it together in one place: a map, a dashboard, a search box. Anyone can open it, with no sign-in, and it can be updated every week as you learn more. The map Places pinned across the metro, filtered by country and kind of place, with an Ask anything bar. pages.d: Tap to Tick is an iPhone expense tracker I designed and built: log any transaction in two taps from the lock screen, including the cash in your pocket. Free, with a shared ledger for two people.
pages.b: Portfolio · App Tap to Tick An iPhone expense tracker: log any transaction in two taps, including the cash in your pocket. App Store See Tap to Tick For Anyone keeping a budget Made Designed and built by me Runs on iPhone and Apple Watch Status Free on the App Store The problem A budget only works if every purchase gets written down. If that means unlocking the phone, hunting for an app or opening a spreadsheet, it does not happen. Cash is the part other apps miss. Pulling $100 from an ATM is not spending. It is moving money from the bank into your pocket. What I built I designed and built the app. It is free on the App Store. A lock-screen widget with today’s running total: raise the phone, tap, enter the amount, pick a category. Three more ways in: Apple Pay, Apple Watch and Siri. Hand-drawn walkthroughs that take a whole letter and put it on one page — who wrote it, what it says, and how the parts fit together. Made for people meeting the book for the first time, in the language they actually think in. Free to watch, free to download, free to show to anyone. ✦ Overview · Ephesians Ephesians A letter from prison. Pick a language below. Both versions are the same walkthrough — same drawings, same order — narrated and lettered in English or Bangla. English বাংলা Bangla Your browser can't play this video. You can download it instead . Ephesians — A Letter from Prison ·3 min 44 sec Download this video What the video covers Written from a prison cell Paul writes to the church in Ephesus while under guard in Rome. Nothing about his circumstances is hidden, and nothing about them dampens the letter. Chapters 1–3 — what God has done Chosen, rescued, and raised with Christ. The first half of the letter is one long look at a gift already given, not a list of things to earn. One new people The wall between Jew and Gentile comes down. Two groups who had every reason to stay apart are made into a single household. Chapters 4–6 — how to walk Believe it, then live like it: unity, honest speech, changed homes and workplaces, and armour for a fight that was never really against people. Why Bangla Roughly 240 million people speak it — and very little of this exists for them. Short, visual overviews of Scripture are easy to find in English and scarce almost everywhere else. Making them in Bangla costs almost nothing once the English version exists, and a four-minute video travels further than a book — it can be watched on a phone, downloaded, and passed on with no internet at all. pages.b: Romans 10:14 · Prayer initiative Pray for the people who still have no one telling them. A simple weekly prayer-meeting kit for the unreached world — a verse, a story, a few facts, and clear prayer points. Free to use, flexible to lead, built so anyone can start a group. See the materials Lead a meeting The verse “How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching?”Romans 10:14 That question is the whole initiative. Most of the world still has almost no access to the gospel. Prayer is where ordinary believers get on the field. What this is A prayer meeting you can actually run. God put a strong desire on one person’s heart to start praying for unreached nations — not once a year, but week by week, with a group. After trying a few approaches, a simple weekly guide stuck. This site is that guide, shared so other people can start the same kind of night where they are. It is not a rigid curriculum. It is a flexible scaffold: enough structure that nobody freezes, enough room that the Holy Spirit still leads. 01 Bible verse A short passage to anchor the night. Ask simple questions — what does this mean for us, why did Jesus say this, how does it land today. 02 Story A real story from the field — missionaries, local believers, or people groups most of us never hear about — so prayer has a face. 03 Missionary quote A short, convicting line from someone who actually went. Useful when the room needs a jolt of courage. 04 Stunning facts Eye-opening numbers about unreached nations, the 10/40 window, and the hard realities of a fallen world. 05 Praise report One place God is already moving — growth, open doors, answered prayer — so the meeting is not only heavy. 06 Prayer points and action Specific asks for the night: a country, a people group, a church under pressure, our own boldness at home — plus one or two practical next steps so the night leaves the room. Unreached A people group with little or no access to the gospel — few believers, no churches of their own, and almost no one telling them about Jesus in a language and culture they understand. The 10/40 window The band of the world from roughly 10° to 40° north latitude across North Africa, the Middle East, and Asia — where most unreached peoples live, and where Christian presence is thinnest. Why I care Romans 10:14 asks a hard question: how will they believe if they never hear? Prayer is not the whole answer — but it is the place most of us can start, and the place the work still needs most. Weekly materials Sample guides you can download tonight. Each PDF is a full meeting: verse, story, quote, facts, praise, prayer points, and one or two action items. Print them, share them, or just open them on a phone in the circle. Iran · underground church Fire in Secret John 1:5, the house church that multiplies under pressure, and prayer for Muslim-background believers. Includes a stylized map, Persian people-group snapshot, and sources. Download PDF → Yemen · transformation Bad Medicine — Great God A missionary family, a medical disaster, and a night of prayer that grew a boy four inches. Prayer points for Yemen, India, Afghanistan, and the church under pressure. Download PDF → North Korea · standing firm Persecution — Perseverance Matthew 5:11–12, the church in North Korea, and what boldness looks like where religious freedom is still a privilege. Includes a people-group snapshot and action items. Download PDF → How to run a night Leader guide The short brief for anyone starting a group: what each weekly guide includes, how to prepare, and the few terms every leader should know. Download PDF → Sample night · Yemen Bad Medicine — Great God A full walkthrough of one weekly guide, so you can see the shape before you download. Verse “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” — John 1:29 Story Around 2000, a missionary family in Yemen was building wells and sharing the gospel. When their son got sick, undertrained doctors gave him the wrong medicine and stunted his growth. One night his parents laid hands on him and prayed — and by morning he had grown roughly four inches back toward normal height. A quiet reminder that God still takes care of His children in the hardest places. (From Sunrise in the Valley of the Shadow of Death by Amira Ann.) Quote “I was called not to comfort or success but to obedience… There is no joy outside of knowing Jesus and serving him.” — Karen Watson Facts Nine years of civil war have gutted Yemen’s health system. A child dies every ten minutes from starvation or easily treatable disease. A woman dies in childbirth every two hours. Almost none of them have ever heard an authentic gospel message. Praise Even under severe persecution, the church in Yemen is growing — about 5.1% a year, compared with roughly 2.6% for the rest of the world. Pray for Yemen’s persecuted church and humanitarian crisis · India (largest unreached population) · Afghanistan · Christian leaders and revival in the West · wars that leave whole regions without a clear gospel witness. Do this Pray for Yemen every day this week. Share one fact about Yemen with another Christian who has never heard it, and ask them to pray too. Download this guide North Korea guide Lead a meeting You do not need a seminary degree. You need a room and a guide. Spend a few minutes in prayer before people arrive. Skim the week’s PDF. Add anything the Spirit puts on your heart. Then let conversation and prayer move naturally — the guide is a help, not a script to finish for its own sake. The aim is simple: encourage one another toward love and good works, grow in Jesus for our joy and His glory, and keep the unreached on the church’s lips. Download the leader guide Email romtenfourteen@icloud.com Pray now One people group. Today. “We can reach our world, if we will. The greatest lack today is not people or funds. The greatest need is prayer.” — Wesley Duewel Joshua Project publishes a different unreached people group every day — population, language, religion, and how to pray. Open it when you have two minutes. Unreached of the day ↗ Why it matters Most of the church prays for what it already sees. The unreached almost never make the prayer list because almost nobody knows their names. A weekly meeting — and one daily people group — is a small way to fix that. Tools Keep the night going after you close in prayer. Unreached of the day Joshua Project’s daily people group — one group, one day, ready to pray for right now.
